title: Clean Coder Blog
summary: Uncle Bob replies to DHH: TDD's ancillary benefits are debatable, but a fast, trusted test suite that enables fearless cleanup is not; GUI tests cannot meet that bar.

assertions.quote: developers can quickly and easily clean the code without fear of breaking anything
Writing tests first requires decoupling that other testing strategies do not
The tests act as accurate, precise, and unambiguous documentation at the lowest level of the system.

verdicts.note: Tests document behaviour but are hard to navigate as documentation; evidence is practitioner opinion.

assertions.quote: you can’t reach all the code from the GUI

verdicts.note: Coverage from end-to-end tests is typically well below unit-level coverage; the 'bit more than half' figure is a guess.

assertions.quote: the benefit of keeping the code clean, and keeping the team moving fast, is so great

verdicts.note: A cost-benefit judgment with no agreed way to measure either side.
